text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 2.2% today, bouncing back after a rough week that saw the stock drop 7.6% from late October highs. The rebound appears tied to refining sector tailwinds: competitors like Chevron, Exxon, and BP all reported earnings beats yesterday on surging refining profits, driven by diesel prices spiking due to geopolitical damage to Russian and Middle Eastern refineries. US refineries are running at 92.8% capacity, and the company also announced a leadership change and update on October 29th, though those details alone don't fully explain today's move.

The stock remains volatile in the near term because the market is still digesting what this week's leadership news means for Marathon's outlook. Refining margins—the profit refiners make by turning crude into fuel—are historically strong right now due to global supply disruptions, which typically benefits Marathon. However, the broader caution flagged by analysts on October 29th suggests investors want to hear concrete forward guidance before fully committing, which may explain why today's bounce is modest despite the sector's strong earnings environment.
